title: AWS Web Application Architecture
summary: Route 53 and CloudFront front an ALB and S3; private EC2 reaches the internet through NAT, is managed by SSM, and monitored by CloudWatch.

nodes.label: Users
nodes.detail: Browsers resolve the domain via DNS and connect over HTTPS.

nodes.label: Route 53
nodes.detail: Resolves the domain name to CloudFront or the load balancer using alias records.

nodes.label: CloudFront
nodes.detail: Caches content at edge locations. Origin Access Control lets only CloudFront read the private S3 bucket.

nodes.label: S3 Bucket
nodes.detail: Private bucket for static files. Public access is blocked; access is granted to CloudFront through OAC.

nodes.label: ALB
nodes.detail: Application load balancer terminating TLS and routing by host or path to targets in private subnets.

nodes.label: NAT Gateway
nodes.detail: Lets private instances reach the internet without inbound exposure. Its Elastic IP can be allow-listed by external services.

nodes.label: Private EC2
nodes.detail: Runs the application with no public IP. Administered through SSM Session Manager rather than open SSH.

nodes.label: SSM, Parameter Store
nodes.detail: Session Manager gives audited shell access. Parameter Store holds configuration and encrypted secrets read via IAM role.

nodes.label: MongoDB Atlas
nodes.detail: Managed database outside AWS whose IP access list permits only the NAT gateway's public address.

nodes.label: CloudWatch
nodes.detail: Collects metrics, logs and alarms from the ALB, instances and other services.

steps.title: DNS directs the user
steps.text: Route 53 resolves the domain to the CloudFront distribution.

steps.title: CloudFront serves the edge
steps.text: Static requests are served from cache or read from S3 via Origin Access Control.

steps.title: Dynamic requests reach the ALB
steps.text: Other paths go to the ALB in the public subnet, which forwards to private instances.

steps.title: Outbound uses NAT
steps.text: The private instance reaches the external database through the NAT gateway, whose IP is allow-listed.

steps.title: Operate and observe
steps.text: SSM provides shell access and Parameter Store config, while CloudWatch collects logs and alarms.
